knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Backwashing is triggered by the gauge or flow reading set in the manual, and the reading should be recorded. A calendar, a request or a noise is not the trigger.
The manual and the handbook both require the pump off because moving the valve under flow damages the valve and its seal. The other reasons are not responsible.
Opening the bleeder releases trapped air before the filter returns to service. Closing it too early leaves air in the system.

practicalCriteria: Trigger, pre-backwash pressure and post-backwash pressure are recorded and the trigger is stated
Valve sequence completed in order, with the pump observed to be off at each valve change
Air bleeder opened and closed in the stated order, with the observer standing clear
A filter that does not clean after backwash is referred with the readings and the reason
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Backwash record from one supervised backwash
Assessor observation sign-off on valve sequence and pump state
Referral note where the filter did not clean
stopWorkCriteria: Valve moved while the pump operates
Filter serviced, opened or tested while under pressure
Air or gas used to test or pressurise the filter
Clamp or valve top forced or modified during backwash
